variants.title: App servers open a connection per request
variants.context: Each HTTP request opens a new Postgres connection and p99 login time on the database climbs.
variants.constraint: The database max_connections is 200 and there are 40 app pods.
variants.question: What is the first fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Reuse a bounded connection pool per process instead of connecting per request.
wrongChoices: Raise max_connections without a pool
Open more connections on every retry
Move SQL into the browser

variants.title: Pool size times replica count
variants.context: Each of 50 pods uses a pool of 50, so the database sees 2,500 connections and refuses new ones.
variants.constraint: Query volume does not need that many sessions.
variants.question: What sizing rule did you miss?
variants.expectedPattern: Size pools so replicas × pool size stays under the database connection budget.
wrongChoices: Set every pool to max_connections
Disable pooling in production
Add more pods to get more connections

variants.title: Checkout waits on a leaked connection
variants.context: A code path forgets to release connections and the pool empties during peak.
variants.constraint: The database still has idle sessions owned by the app.
variants.question: What operational pattern prevents the stall?
variants.expectedPattern: Always return connections (try/finally or pool checkout), plus leak detection and timeouts.
wrongChoices: Grow the pool forever
Restart Postgres on every leak
Share one connection across threads with no lock

variants.title: Idle transactions hold locks
variants.context: A pooled connection stays in an open transaction while the app waits on a vendor API.
variants.question: What should not happen on a pooled connection?
variants.expectedPattern: Do not hold a database transaction across slow external I/O; commit or rollback before waiting.
wrongChoices: Keep the transaction open during the HTTP timeout
Disable idle_in_transaction timeouts
Increase lock_timeout to hours

variants.title: Serverless cold start storm
variants.context: Lambda concurrency jumps to 500 and each runtime opens its own DB connections.
variants.constraint: The database cannot accept 500 simultaneous handshakes.
variants.question: What sits between functions and Postgres?
variants.expectedPattern: A connection proxy or pooled gateway so short-lived runtimes share a small set of DB sessions.
wrongChoices: One connection per concurrent invocation with no proxy
Disable function concurrency
Embed Postgres in each Lambda package

variants.title: Health check uses a real query connection
variants.context: Load balancer probes check out a pool connection and run a heavy query.
variants.constraint: Probes run every 2 seconds on every pod.
variants.question: How should probes treat the pool?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a cheap ping or a dedicated lightweight check that does not starve the request pool.
wrongChoices: SELECT * FROM a large table on every probe
Check out all pool connections for the probe
Skip database health entirely

variants.title: Read and write share one exhausted pool
variants.context: Analytics reports occupy every connection, so checkouts cannot write orders.
variants.question: How do you isolate traffic?
variants.expectedPattern: Separate pools (or a replica) for reports versus transactional writes.
wrongChoices: One pool with no timeout for both workloads
Let reports hold connections indefinitely
Kill the primary to free sessions

variants.title: Stale connections after failover
variants.context: The primary fails over, but pooled sockets still point at the old node and errors persist.
variants.constraint: The pool does not validate on checkout.
variants.question: What pool behavior is required?
variants.expectedPattern: Validate or recycle connections after errors and failover so clients reach the new primary.
wrongChoices: Keep dead sockets until process restart
Disable TCP keepalive
Retry forever on the old IP

variants.title: Thread pool vs DB pool mismatch
variants.context: 200 servlet threads each wait on a 10-connection DB pool.
variants.constraint: Most threads sit blocked on checkout.
variants.question: What is the mismatch?
variants.expectedPattern: Align request concurrency with pool size, or fail fast when the pool is exhausted.
wrongChoices: Unbounded servlet threads waiting on checkout
Set DB pool size to 1 for 200 threads
Remove checkout timeouts

variants.title: PgBouncer transaction vs session mode
variants.context: The app uses session-level SET and prepared statements, but the proxy is in transaction pooling mode.
variants.question: What must match?
variants.expectedPattern: Pooling mode must match how the app uses session state, or the app must be session-stateless.
wrongChoices: Ignore pooling mode
SET role on a connection and return it without reset
Disable the proxy and hope

variants.title: Redis unbounded clients
variants.context: Each worker opens Redis connections in a loop until the instance hits maxclients.
variants.constraint: Work is bursty but connections are never reused.
variants.question: What Redis access pattern is correct?
variants.expectedPattern: A bounded Redis connection pool (or multiplexed client) shared by the process.
wrongChoices: connect() on every cache get
One global static connection used from many threads without a safe client
Disable Redis maxclients

variants.title: Checkout timeout too long
variants.context: When the pool is empty, requests wait 60 seconds for a connection.
variants.question: What should the pool do under saturation?
variants.expectedPattern: Fail checkout quickly with a clear error so the request can shed or retry elsewhere.
wrongChoices: Block the user thread for a full minute
Grow the pool past database limits
Return 200 with empty data

variants.title: Overnight idle disconnects
variants.context: The firewall drops idle TCP after 5 minutes and the first morning request fails.
variants.constraint: The pool still thinks sockets are live.
variants.question: How do you keep pooled connections healthy?
variants.expectedPattern: Idle timeouts, validation queries, or keepalives shorter than the network idle drop.
wrongChoices: Infinite idle lifetime
No TCP keepalive
Reconnect only after a customer pages you

variants.title: ORM opens a second hidden pool
variants.context: The app already pools via a proxy, but the ORM also opens 20 connections per pod.
variants.constraint: Two layers of pooling multiply sessions.
variants.question: What is the design mistake?
variants.expectedPattern: Have a single pooling layer with a known size; do not stack unbounded pools.
wrongChoices: Pool at ORM, sidecar, and database with no budget
Disable the proxy and also disable the ORM pool
Set both pools to max_connections

variants.title: Migration job starves the site
variants.context: A schema migration uses 80 connections from the same app pool as web traffic.
variants.constraint: Users still need to check out.
variants.question: How should the job get connections?
variants.expectedPattern: A separate, capped pool (or a maintenance window) so migrations cannot empty the web pool.
wrongChoices: Share the web pool with no cap for DDL
max_connections for the migrator
Run migrations inside each user request
